_comment: What the meadow gives up, and to which tool. CONTENT for the left-hand column (which prop is which kind), TUNABLE for every number. MEADOWS_VERTICAL_SLICE.md M8: 'Minimal materials only — Wood, Stone, Fiber, Berries'. There is nothing here that comes off a creature, and there must never be: GAME_DESIGN.md 19 forbids a hunting economy outright and CLAUDE.md repeats it as a hard rule.
_comment_firewall: What an ITEM is lives in data/items/items.json. What a BUILD PIECE costs lives on the piece in data/building/pieces.json. This file is the third relationship — what a PROP yields — and it is here rather than in either of those because a harvest is a relationship between a thing in the world and an item, and neither of those files describes two things at once.
_comment_no_nodes: The props are drawn as MultiMesh instances — around 70,000 of them across the meadow at the time of writing — and a MultiMesh instance is an index, not a node. scripts/world/harvestable.gd builds a spatial hash from the batches themselves rather than giving every tree a node; the `models` lists below are how a batch is recognised, because a batch is named after the model it draws.
_comment_cell: TUNABLE. Spatial hash cell size in metres. Bigger cells mean fewer buckets and more props to scan inside each one; 4m is about two strides and puts a handful of props in a bucket in the thickest grove.
_comment_reach: TUNABLE. How far in front of the trainer a swing can find something, in metres. Deliberately shorter than build reach (9m): you build at arm's length plus a bit, but you chop what you are standing at.
_comment_model_match: A batch node is named after its model, plus a `_x_y` suffix when vegetation.gd splits it into spatial cells. Matching is by LONGEST model name the node name starts with, which is what keeps `Bush_Common_Flowers` (berries) from being read as `Bush_Common` (fiber).
_comment_depletion: THE MODEL: a prop DEPLETES and REGROWS; it is not consumed and the forest does not thin out. `uses` swings empty it, `regrow` seconds bring it back. See docs/decisions/D19 for why nothing vanishes.
_comment_uses: TUNABLE. `amount` is the yield PER SWING and `uses` is how many swings the prop has in it, so a tree is worth amount x uses in total. `durability` is what one swing costs the tool, in the units items.json counts.
_comment_tool: `tool` is the item id a swing needs. An empty string means bare hands. `hand_amount`/`hand_uses`, where present, are what BARE HANDS get from a prop that has a proper tool — the tool improves the yield rather than being a key. Trees and boulders have no hand entry on purpose: punching a tree is the survival-game cliche this design does not want, and durability only means something if the tool is the only way in.

tree._comment: The wood supply. Four swings of an axe, twelve wood, and seven minutes before that tree is worth visiting again — so a cottage is six trees and a short walk rather than one tree and a loading bar.

deadfall._comment: The bootstrap. Dead standing timber you can break up by hand, so a trainer with an empty inventory can reach a workbench and a first axe without punching a living tree. Four wood a piece and only 55 of them in the meadow, which is enough to start and nowhere near enough to build with.

rock._comment: The stone supply. Same shape as a tree, and deliberately scarcer: 203 boulders against 288 trees, so stone is the material a stone-built cottage is actually gated on.

pebble._comment: The other half of the bootstrap: loose stones you pick up. One stone each and 66 in the meadow, which pays for a workbench and a knife and then stops mattering.

bush._comment: Fiber. The one kind where the tool is an UPGRADE rather than a key — bare hands tear one fiber off, a knife takes three twice over. That is what makes the knife worth crafting without making fiber unreachable before you have one, which would deadlock the whole recipe chain.

berry_bush._comment: GAME_DESIGN.md 21's foraging half. Bare hands, one pass, three berries, back in three minutes. Bush_Common_Flowers is a STAND-IN: the Quaternius nature pack has no berry bush, and the flowering bush is the closest silhouette in the meadow. 195 of them, so a berry run is a real trip and the berry plot is still worth building.

_comment_not_here: Grass, flowers, clover, mushrooms, path stones and the village buildings are NOT harvestable and are not in the lists above. Grass alone is 61,000 instances; indexing it would multiply the spatial hash by twenty-five to sell fiber that bushes already sell better. Mushrooms are left out because they read as food and M9 owns food; a mushroom that yielded fiber would be a lie about what it is.
